explanation: Mixture: fires on the closing ')' of 'Copyright (c)', on 'to' after 'begin/start(ed)', on '/or' in 'and/or', and on mid-word subword pieces of names and acronyms (car[pal], One[Web], J[PY], Ta[ft], State[ College]). No single shared feature; outside these patterns activation is weak.

Fires on mid-word subword fragments inside words that are split into many pieces: misspelled or oddly hyphenated English, non-English words (Norwegian, Romanian, Finnish, Albanian, German, Hindi, Japanese), and unusual names (us[i]ng, til[legg], More[ver], parl[iment]). Whole common English words give little or nothing.

Mixture of unrelated triggers: 'Minister' after 'Prime', 'undefeated', 'amnesia', 'allegedly', and subword pieces of domain/package names (stackpath, .jetbrains, googleusercontent, Xunit) and proper names (Taliban, Tahitian, Alban). Strongest on a handful of specific lexical items, not a shared concept.

Mostly fires on tokens in code and boilerplate structure, especially import lists (Go import package strings like "errors", import ending quotes/newlines, require('os'), #include <errno.h>), plus scattered boilerplate phrases ('One of the following', 'Code Generator', 'SUMMARY ORDER', legal citations). Activation is broad across structured/technical text with no tight concept.

Fires on 'and' (or a comma) joining items in a list of names, especially lists of judges in court opinions ('Before X, Y, and Z'), firm/company names ('Morgan Stanley, BofA Merrill Lynch and Mizuho'), and other legal-header tokens. Strongest when the coordinated items are proper names in legal/financial text.

Fires on the first subword piece(s) of a word that gets split into multiple tokens, mainly scientific/technical terms (Maxwell-B[oltzmann], ant[io]xygenic, [o]ocyte, [o]phthalmology, pl[as]minogen) and foreign words/names. The token is an incomplete word start whose continuation is predictable from context.

Mixture: space between CSS padding values ('padding: 0 0'), the 'block' piece of 'beta-blocker', 'antico[ag]ulant', absorption/absorb, 'Rew[rite]Rule', '__esModule', and assorted compound-word second pieces (monoclon[al], Volley[ball], peer[ reviewed]). Several unrelated specific lexical triggers.

Mainly fires on attribute/keyword tokens inside HTML/XML/code markup that follow a tag or type name, e.g. ' class' in <li class=, ' src' in <script type=... src=, ' android' attribute, ' struct', '<option', and repeated list elements; plus a few odd prose tokens ('over', 'TIME'). Strongest in repetitive markup.

Fires on the punctuation that opens a citation/footnote marker right after the end of a claim in academic or wiki text: ' ([' before '@B3]', '.[' before '1]', '[@', '.^'. Moderate on other sentence-final punctuation and numbers; near zero elsewhere.

Fires on ' (' opening an acronym definition after a spelled-out name ('Growth hormone (GH)', 'Integration Host Factor (IHF)'), and also on interior subword pieces of identifiers, usernames, numbers and names (shfsh[any]ue, 514[8]8, google[bot]). Two loosely related jobs around naming/identifier tokens.

Fires on the first token of a top-level declaration in C/C++/Objective-C code, such as 'class', 'enum', 'static', 'public', 'char', following a blank line or namespace/include block, and on '[' starting an Objective-C message send after '='. Weak in other code or prose.

Fires on a non-initial subword piece of a proper noun or acronym, especially names starting a paragraph or sentence (Rich[mond], Ab[dess]amad, NO[AA], Trip[Advisor], Huckabee, L[GPL], LL[VM]). Common words get little activation.

Fires on nouns describing natural landscape, water and outdoor/environmental features, usually the second word of a compound (river banks, sea level, ocean currents, mountain stream, wind turbines, River Thames, pine trees, warm waters). Weak on other text.

Fires on words about a person's own body, identity or self (robot form, severed heads, themselves/himself/myself, height and weight, identifiable/identity information, 'births' in 'Category:1992 births'), often in violent or personal contexts. Loose theme of the self/person as object.

Mixture: closing letters of acronyms in parentheses (D[CT], Mo[Abs], ddI[)]), variables in algebra word problems ('-3[*f]', '[*j]'), 'extends' in PHP class declarations, and common function words (the, as, of, other). No single shared trigger.

Fires on the word that names a form or format after 'in', especially ' binary' in BSD license text ('Redistributions in binary form'), and more weakly on 'the'/other words in 'in the form of', 'in paperback', 'in game format', 'in any form'. Predicts an upcoming 'form/format'.

Fires on the first fragment of a word broken into subword pieces, particularly in non-English text (Czech, Finnish, Danish, Spanish, French) and in words like O-phthalmology or o-ocyte, plus short Romance clitics ('se', 'il'). The token is an incomplete word start or a short function word in foreign-language text.

Diffuse: fires on many ordinary tokens in conversational or first-person text (I, am, is, to, bed, roll) and on scattered code/legal tokens ('Court of', include paths). No clear shared feature beyond common mid-sentence tokens.

Fires on the second or later subword piece of technical or domain-specific words (basophil[ic], scintill[ators], ord[ained], muscar[inic], granz[yme], left[-handed]) and on a few function words in fixed phrases ('trails ... by', 'worse ... than', 'Certiorari granted'). Mostly completion of a predictable multi-token term.

Two jobs: digits inside patent or application numbers ('Patent Application No. 5[7]-', 'JP 200[6]-158', 'EP-A-4[5]977'), and the first subword piece of a split word ('co'-struzione, co-opted, lo-yally, ra-ucous, for-ças). Both are early pieces of a token sequence that continues.

Fires on the main verb of a clause right after its subject noun phrase, in any language (Rusland vol[gt], photographer make, statement points, column states, Volunteers bring, functions return). Strongest on present-tense finite verbs following a full subject.
